name: Keep a consistent sleep schedule
requirements: Choose realistic bed and wake times
description: Go to bed and get up at the same times each day, including weekends.
caution: Adjust gradually if your current schedule is very different or if a clinician has given you a different sleep plan.

name: Keep daytime naps to 10 minutes or less
requirements: Timer if helpful
description: Avoid longer daytime naps so nighttime sleep is more likely.
caution: This may not fit everyone, especially people with medical fatigue, hypersomnia, shift work, or clinician-directed rest needs.

name: Use the bed only for sleep
requirements: Another place for reading, phone use, or TV
description: Avoid using the bed during the day for TV, phone calls, reading, or other wakeful activities.
caution: Adapt for disability, pain, limited housing, or situations where bed is the only accessible place.

name: Avoid late caffeine, nicotine, alcohol, heavy meals, and exercise
requirements: Alternative drinks, snacks, or activity plans
description: Reduce substances, meals, and intense activity that may interfere with sleep late in the day.
caution: Medication timing, substance dependence, eating needs, and medical conditions may require individualized guidance.

name: Cool, quiet, dark room setup
requirements: Lighting, fan, eye mask, earplugs, white noise, bedding
description: Turn off lights, keep the room quiet, and make the temperature comfortable and relatively cool.
caution: Use sensory tools that are safe and personally tolerable. Do not use earplugs or white noise if they increase distress or reduce needed awareness.

name: Use warmth if cold
requirements: Blanket, warm socks, or safely used electric blanket
description: Add safe warmth if being cold is keeping you awake.
caution: Avoid overheating, burns, or unsafe heating devices. Follow product directions and medical guidance.

name: Use cooling if hot
requirements: Fan, lighter bedding, or feet outside blanket
description: Cool the sleep environment if heat is keeping you awake.
caution: Consider cold sensitivity, autonomic conditions, pain, or other medical needs.

name: Give sleep 30–60 minutes
requirements: Clock out of direct view if clock-checking increases pressure
description: Allow half an hour to at most an hour to fall asleep, then assess whether you are calm, anxious, or ruminating.
caution: Avoid repeatedly checking the clock if that increases anxiety.

name: Aim for rest, not perfect sleep
requirements: A reassuring phrase
description: Remind yourself that rest still matters and that being awake is not a catastrophe.
caution: This is not meant to dismiss severe or persistent insomnia.

name: Get out of bed for a quiet activity
requirements: Another dim, quiet space and low-stimulation activity
description: Leave the bed and do something that will not wake you further. Return when tired or sleepy.
caution: Use fall precautions, mobility supports, and safe lighting as needed.

name: Read a low-stimulation book
requirements: Book and dim light
description: Read something that is not overly stimulating until you begin to feel sleepy.
caution: Avoid bright screens or content that increases alertness.

name: Have a light snack
requirements: A light, tolerated snack
description: Try a small snack, such as an apple or another personally appropriate option.
caution: Adapt for reflux, diabetes, allergies, eating disorders, medication instructions, and other medical needs.

name: Cold-water TIP skill
requirements: Cold water and established TIP instructions
description: Use the cold-water TIP skill, then return to bed.
caution: The handout specifically says to get medical approval before using cold water if you have any medical condition.

name: Paced breathing in bed
requirements: Comfortable position
description: After returning to bed, use paced breathing without forcing the breath.
caution: Stop if breath focus increases panic, dizziness, air hunger, numbness, or discomfort.

name: 9–0 meditation
requirements: None
description: Count down on each slow exhale from 9 to 0, then begin again from 8, then 7, continuing until starting from 1.
caution: If counting becomes frustrating, use a simpler repeated count or another calming anchor.

name: Notice the body sensation beneath rumination
requirements: A tolerable level of body awareness
description: Notice where the worry shows up physically instead of continuing only in thought.
caution: Body focus can intensify trauma, panic, pain, dysphoria, or health anxiety. Switch to external grounding if needed.

name: Label it middle-of-the-night thinking
requirements: A prepared reminder
description: Remind yourself that nighttime worries often feel different in the morning.
caution: Do not use this to ignore an immediate safety, medical, or practical emergency.

name: Read an emotionally engrossing novel, then continue it in your head
requirements: A novel and dim light
description: Read briefly until somewhat tired, then close your eyes and continue imagining the story.
caution: Choose content that is engaging but not activating or frightening.

name: If solvable, solve it briefly
requirements: Paper or notes app
description: Identify one practical next step, write it down, and stop working on it for the night.
caution: Avoid turning this into a long planning session that increases alertness.

name: If unsolvable, cope ahead
requirements: Familiarity with cope-ahead practice
description: Imagine the feared outcome, then imagine yourself coping with it step by step.
caution: This can intensify distress or intrusive imagery. Stop if arousal rises and return to grounding or professional support.

name: Listen to low-volume public radio or steady spoken audio
best_for: When other methods have not worked
requirements: Low-volume radio, podcast, or steady spoken audio; headphones if needed
description: Listen with eyes closed to speech with little fluctuation in tone or volume.
caution: Keep volume safe and avoid upsetting, stimulating, or autoplay-driven content.
